source_text:
καὶ ὑποβεβηκότως καὶ ὑφειμένως τε ἔτι. «Ἀστὴρ γὰρ ἀστέρος διαφέρει ἐν δόξῃ·» καὶ παρ' αὐτοῖς δέ φημι τοῖς ἁγίοις ἀγγέλοις, ἐν διαφοραῖς εἶναι πολλαῖς τῆς εὐκλείας τὸ μέτρον, πλὴν ἐν οἷσπερ ἂν εἴη μέτροις, ἡ τῶν ἁγίων ζωὴ, τὸ ἱλαρὸν ἔχει· καὶ τὸ δ' εὐθυμεῖσθαι δεῖν, καὶ καταπιαίνεσθαι τοῖς παρὰ Θεοῦ. Ἄθρει γὰρ ὅπως τὸ ἔλαιον οὐχὶ μόνοις τοῖς τρισὶν ἐπεχεῖτο δεκάτοις, ἀλλὰ καὶ δυσὶ, καὶ ἑνί. Ἐνδελεχισμοῦ δὲ θυσίαν καὶ ὁλοκαυτώματα, καλεῖ τὸν ἀμνὸν τὸν σφαγιαζόμενον ἐν τῇ ἁγίᾳ σκηνῇ τὸ πρωῒ, καὶ ἀγχοῦ πρὸς ἑσπέραν. Δι' οὗ δὴ πάλιν ἐξέσται μαθεῖν, ὅτι πολὺ τὸ εὐῶδες τῆς ἁγίας σκηνῆς, καὶ ἀκατάληκτος ἀληθῶς, ἡ τῶν Ἐκκλησιῶν εὐοσμία, καὶ τῶν ἐν αὐταῖς ἁγίων. Εὐωδιάζουσι γὰρ τὸν Ἐμμανουὴλ, καὶ τὸ ἐπὶ Χριστῷ τελοῦσι μυστήριον τὴν ἀναίμακτον λατρείαν προσκομίζοντες τῷ Θεῷ. Τοῦτο γὰρ, οἶμαι, ἐστὶ τὸ πρωΐ τε καὶ πρὸς ἑσπέραν ὁλοκαυτίζεσθαι τοὺς ἀμνούς. Ἀρχῇ γὰρ καὶ τέλει, καὶ διὰ μέσου λαμβάνεται. Οὐκοῦν ἀπαρχῆς μέχρι τέλους τὸ εὐῶδες ἐν Ἐκκλησίαις, ὡς ἐν ἀμνῷ τῷ Χριστῷ.
{ΠΑΛΛ.} Εὖ ἔφης.
{ΚΥΡ.} Ἑτέραν δὲ αὖ νόμος ἐπισυνάπτει τῇ πρώτῃ τὴν ἑορτὴν, μονονουχὶ δὲ καὶ αὐτοὺς ἡμῖν τοὺς καιροὺς συνείρει λέγων ἐν τοῖς Ἀριθμοῖς· «Καὶ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῶν νέων, ὅταν προσφέρητε θυσίαν νέαν Κυρίῳ τῶν ἑβδομάδων, ἐπίκλητος ἁγία ἔσται ὑμῖν, πᾶν ἔργον λατρευτὸν οὐ ποιήσετε. Καὶ προσάξετε ὁλοκαυτώματα εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας Κυρίῳ, μόσχους ἐκ βοῶν δύο, κριὸν ἕνα, ἀμνοὺς ἐνιαυσίους ἑπτὰ ἀμώμους. Ἡ θυσία αὐτῶν σεμίδαλις ἀναπεποιημένη ἐν ἐλαίῳ, τρία δέκατα τῷ μόσχῳ τῷ ἑνὶ, καὶ δύο δέκατα τῷ κριῷ τῷ ἑνὶ, δέκατον δέκατον τῷ ἀμνῷ τῷ ἑνὶ, τοῖς ἑπτὰ ἀμνοῖς, καὶ χίμαρον ἐξ αἰγῶν ἕνα περὶ ἁμαρτίας, ἐξιλάσασθαι περὶ ὑμῶν, πλὴν τοῦ ὁλοκαυτώματος τοῦ διαπαντός. Καὶ τὴν θυσίαν αὐτῶν ποιήσετέ μοι, ἄμωμοι ἔσονται ὑμῖν, καὶ τὰς σπονδὰς αὐτῶν.» Ἐν μηνὶ μὲν γὰρ τῷ πρώτῳ, κατὰ τοὺς Ἑβραίων νόμους, ὁ ἀμνὸς ἐσφάζετο. Τῷ δὲ ἀγχοῦ τάχα που καὶ γείτονι, συναγείρειν ἔθος τὰ ἐξ ἀγρῶν, ὀσπρίων δὴ λέγω τὰ πρώϊμα, καὶ δέσμην ἀμάλλης, ἀμηθέντος ἤδη καὶ σίτου. Καιρὸς οὖν ἄρα τῶν νέων, καθ' ὃν ἐξ ἀγρῶν συναγείρεσθαι χρὴ, τὰ ἐν αὐτοῖς ἐσπαρμένα. Κλητὴ δὲ πάλιν ἡ τοιάδε, φησὶν, ἑορτὴ, καὶ περαινέσθω συννόμως, πόνου καὶ ἱδρῶτος ἐξῃρημένον. Ἀνεῖσθαι γὰρ ἔθος ἐν ἑορταῖς καὶ ἀποφοιτᾷν ὅτι μάλιστα τῶν ἐργωδεστέρων. Ἀναμάθοι δ' ἄν τις κἀκ τοῦδε δὴ πάλιν, ὅτι τοὺς ἁγίαν τῷ Θεῷ τελοῦντας τὴν ἑορτὴν, πρέποι ἂν ἥκιστά γε, τὴν ἀκλεᾶ καὶ παμμόχθηρον πληροῦν ἁμαρτίαν. Ἀνέντας δὲ ὥσπερ καὶ πληροῦντας τὸν νοῦν, τοῖς εἰς ἀρετὴν ἐντρυφᾷν σπουδάσμασι. Προσφέρονται δὲ καὶ εἰς ὁλοκαύτωμα καὶ θυσίαν, μόσχοι μὲν δύο, κριὸς δὲ εἷς καὶ ἑπτὰ ἀμνοὶ, σεμίδαλις ἐλαιοβραχὴς, καὶ χίμαρος ἐξ αἰγῶν. Καὶ ὅποι ποτὲ βλέποι τοῦ νόμου τὸ αἴνιγμα, διειρηκότες ἀρτίως, οὐ ταυτολογήσομεν. Πλὴν, ἐκεῖνο ἐροῦμεν ἀναγκαίως, ὅτι τῆς τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν ἀναστά
pass_a_gloss: (and to some) also in a lower and still more lowered way. For star differs from star in glory; and among the holy angels themselves, I say, the measure of the glory is in many differences, but in whatever measures it may be, the life of the saints has the cheerful; and also that (they) must be in good spirits and be fattened with the things from God. For look how the oil was poured not on the three tenths only, but also on two and on one. And the sacrifice and whole burnt offerings of continuance he calls the lamb slaughtered in the holy tent in the morning and near toward evening. Through which again it will be possible to learn that the fragrance of the holy tent is much, and truly unceasing is the sweet odor of the Churches and of the saints in them. For they are fragrant of Emmanuel and complete the mystery about Christ, bringing to God the bloodless worship. For this, I think, is the being made whole burnt offerings of the lambs in the morning and toward evening. For it is taken by beginning and end, and through the middle. Therefore from the firstfruit until the end the fragrance is in the Churches, as in the lamb, Christ. PALLADIUS: You said well. CYRIL: And another feast in turn the law joins to the first, and all but links together for us the seasons themselves, saying in the Numbers: And on the day of the new (things), when you bring a new sacrifice to the Lord, of the weeks, it will be for you called holy, every servile work you will not do. And you will bring whole burnt offerings for an odor of fragrance to the Lord, calves from oxen two, ram one, lambs yearly seven blameless. Their sacrifice fine flour worked up in oil, three tenths to the one calf, and two tenths to the one ram, a tenth a tenth to the one lamb, for the seven lambs, and one goat from goats concerning sin, to propitiate concerning you, besides the whole burnt offering of the continual. And you will make their sacrifice for me, they will be blameless for you, and their libations. For in the first month, according to the laws of the Hebrews, the lamb was slaughtered. And in the near and perhaps neighboring one, (it was) custom to gather the things from fields, I mean the early ones of pulses, and a sheaf, the wheat having already been reaped. Season then of the new things, according to which it is necessary to gather from fields the things sown in them. And called again (is) such a feast, he says, and let it be accomplished lawfully, taken out of toil and sweat. For it is custom in feasts to be relaxed and to depart as much as possible from the more laborious things. And someone might learn again also from this, that for those completing a holy feast to God, it would be least fitting to fulfill the inglorious and all-wicked sin. But, having relaxed as it were and filling the mind, to luxuriate in the zeals toward virtue. And there are brought for whole burnt offering and sacrifice calves two, and one ram and seven lambs, fine flour oil-wetted, and a goat from goats. And wherever the riddle of the law looks, having explained just now, we will not say the same again. Except we will say that necessarily, that of the resurrection of our Savior (continues).
pass_b_english: Cyril: … a lower and still humbler one. ‘For star differs from star in glory’ (1 Corinthians 15:41). Even among the holy angels themselves, I say, the measure of glory comes in many degrees; yet whatever the measure, the life of the saints is full of gladness, and they must be of good cheer and be richly fed with the gifts of God. For see how the oil was poured not only on the three tenths, but on the two and on the one as well. And the lamb slaughtered in the holy tent in the morning and again toward evening he calls the sacrifice and whole burnt offerings of perpetuity. From this, again, we may learn that great is the fragrance of the holy tent, and truly unceasing is the sweet savor of the churches and of the saints in them. For they give off the fragrance of Emmanuel and perform the mystery of Christ, bringing the bloodless worship to God. This, I think, is what the offering of the lambs as whole burnt offerings in the morning and toward evening means: by the beginning and the end, what lies between is understood as well. So from first to last there is fragrance in the churches, as in the lamb, Christ.

Cyril: To the first feast the law joins another, and all but links the very seasons together for us, saying in Numbers: ‘And on the day of the new crops, when you offer a new sacrifice of weeks to the Lord, it shall be called holy for you; you shall do no servile work. And you shall offer whole burnt offerings for a fragrant aroma to the Lord: two calves from the herd, one ram, seven lambs a year old, without blemish. Their sacrifice shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths for the one calf, and two tenths for the one ram, a tenth, a tenth for each lamb, for the seven lambs; and one male goat for sin, to make propitiation for you, besides the continual whole burnt offering. And you shall make their sacrifice for me (they shall be without blemish for you), and their drink offerings’ (Numbers 28:26–31).

In the first month, by the laws of the Hebrews, the lamb was slaughtered. In the next, the neighboring month perhaps, it was the custom to gather in the produce of the fields, I mean the early pulses, and the sheaf, once the wheat had been reaped. So this is the season of the new crops, at which what was sown in the fields must be gathered in. And such a feast, he says, is ‘called’ as well, and it is to be carried through according to the law, free from toil and sweat. For it is the custom at feasts to rest and to keep as far as possible from the more laborious kinds of work. And from this one might learn again that for those who keep a holy feast to God it would be least of all fitting to commit inglorious and utterly wicked sin; rather they should, as it were, rest and fill the mind, and take their delight in the pursuits of virtue. And there are offered as whole burnt offering and sacrifice two calves, one ram and seven lambs, fine flour moistened with oil, and a male goat. Where the riddle of the law points, we explained just now; we will not repeat ourselves. But this we must say: that of our Savior’s resurrection …

choices.term: Ἀρχῇ γὰρ καὶ τέλει, καὶ διὰ μέσου λαμβάνεται
choices.english: by the beginning and the end, what lies between is understood as well
choices.why: Morning and evening stand for the whole day; the gloss keeps the logic.
ἀπαρχή here pairs with τέλος as ‘first’; not the ‘firstfruits’ offering.
The word is split at the column break; it is rendered once, here, and the sentence goes on in §17.
